history.content: who maintained power in the governments of the colonies?

The three forms of colonial governments were provincial ( royal colony ), proprietary, and charter. In royal colonies, the king appointed the governor, while in proprietary colonies, lord proprietors appointed the governor. In charter colonies, grantees were given control of the land and the powers of legislative government through letters patent. However, it's important to note that all these forms of government were subordinate to the King of England with no representation in the Parliament of Great Britain.
What gave rise to salve labor in these colonies?

The increased difficulty in recruiting labor due to improved economic conditions and easing of religious persecution in Europe led to the colonies becoming increasingly reliant on slave labor, particularly in the South. Slavery was legal and of economic importance in the export-oriented tobacco plantations of Virginia and Maryland and on the rice and indigo plantations of South Carolina. Some of the colonies developed legalized systems of slavery, centered largely around the Atlantic slave trade with about 287,000 slaves imported into the Thirteen Colonies over 160 years. The great majority went to sugar colonies in the Caribbean and to Brazil, where life expectancy was short and the numbers had to be continually replenished. The growth of the slave population in British North America was dramatic between 1680 and 1750, supporting vast plantation economies in the South, while slaves in the North worked in various occupations.
